findings.title: [P1] Restrict post-login redirects to trusted destinations
findings.body: When `returnUrl` comes from a request parameter, values such as `https://attacker.example` or `//attacker.example` redirect authenticated users to an arbitrary origin. Validate this as an allowed same-origin path before calling `location.assign`.

findings.title: [P1] Remove issued tokens from audit output
findings.body: `recordIssuedToken` passes the raw credential to `audit`, which writes its detail argument directly to `console.log`. Any operator or system with log access can replay a still-valid token and impersonate its owner; log non-sensitive metadata instead.

findings.title: [P3] Apply the anonymous fallback after trimming
findings.body: For a whitespace-only cached value, `trim()` produces `""`, which bypasses the nullish fallback and returns a blank display name. Fall back after normalization if blank names are not valid.

findings.title: [P1] Reject untrusted redirect schemes and origins
findings.body:
When `returnUrl` is attacker-controlled, values such as `https://evil.example` create an open redirect after login; `javascript:` URLs may also execute in the authenticated origin where CSP does not block them.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P1] Do not write issued bearer tokens to audit logs
findings.body:
Every real token passed to `recordIssuedToken` is sent verbatim to `console.log`. In environments that collect application console output, anyone with log access can recover active credentials and impersonate users.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P2] Apply the anonymous fallback after trimming
findings.body:
For a whitespace-only cached value such as `{user: "   "}`, `trim()` produces `""`, which is not nullish, so the function returns a blank name instead of `"Anonymous"`.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P1] Remove issued tokens from audit output
findings.body:
Every call writes the raw token to `console.log`; in deployments where console output is retained or accessible to operators/support systems, anyone with log access can replay a still-valid bearer or session token and take over the associated account.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P2] Restrict post-login redirects to trusted same-origin URLs
findings.body:
An attacker-controlled `returnUrl`, such as `https://attacker.example/phish` or `//attacker.example`, now sends authenticated users to an arbitrary origin. Any login flow that sources this argument from a request/query parameter becomes an open redirect suitable for trusted-domain phishing.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._
